notes: The first-party governance proposal moves the legacy Goldfinch protocol into recovery-only maintenance mode and winds down Goldfinch Prime. A 7 July update states that Prime investors were fully redeemed, no new deposits are accepted, and the contract was paused, while legacy V1 borrower pools remain in payment or recovery. Review whether Goldfinch Prime should be modeled as a historically significant institutional-yield product/platform exception, whether legacy V1 and Prime remain one platform entity, and how customer outcomes should be scoped by product.

major_event: Platform-wide orderly wind-down with Earn, staking, lending, and other products scheduled for phased discontinuation and product-specific redemption or settlement arrangements still pending

duplicate_check.notes: No BitMart canonical CYA platform was found in the current repository review. A full candidate audit remains required before any promotion.

notes: BitMart announced an orderly wind-down on 26 July 2026. The notice schedules the end of spot, futures, and other trading on 26 August 2026 and formal trading-platform termination on 31 January 2027. It also states that BitMart Earn, Staking, Lending, Launchpad, and other products will be discontinued in phases, with dedicated redemption, settlement, and follow-up procedures to be communicated to affected users. Generic exchange Earn products are not prioritized in CYA, so BitMart is staged rather than promoted. Review whether the platform-wide shutdown and unresolved product-level customer outcomes justify a historically significant exchange-Earn exception, identify each affected yield or lending product, preserve product-specific custody and terms, and do not infer repayment completion before official settlement evidence is available.

duplicate_check.notes: Repository name, alias and domain review found no canonical AQRU or Accru Finance record. Scanner and candidate audit remain mandatory before promotion.

notes: AQRU is in CYA scope as a custodial consumer-facing crypto-yield platform with a documented launch, operating scale, yield reductions, ownership transfer and currently narrowed product availability. The proposed limited status reflects that several legacy products are closed to new deposits and access now uses a USD 250,000 minimum, while the site still presents at least one yield product and exchange functionality. Do not classify the 2023 transfer to Langland as customer loss or platform failure. Canonical review must distinguish historical Flex and Maple products, the current Real-World Receivables product, custody and loan language in the terms, and the lack of any verified universal customer-outcome event.
